notes: The prompt self-declares a 3D platformer and the glide, charge and double-jump movement is the game, so Obby & Platformer leads; Adventure is genuinely the second thing here, since gems, eggs, hidden alcoves and freeing trapped dragons are a collectathon exploration loop, and it lends alcove-secret and gate-progression that Obby could not express. Precision Platformer is the matching preset for an open 3D playground platformer, kept for obstacle-jump and path-shortcut but with obstacle-moving dropped, because a prompt this exhaustive about its movement verbs never mentions moving platforms. I replaced the preset's course-terraced with world-hub-dungeon from the catalogue, since the author confirmed a safe central hub feeding five district-sized realms through portals, which is P4 for the separate maps and P3 for entering enclosed places like the lava caverns; the P4 override does not apply because the prompt asks for separate maps rather than one continuous world. Two things for the pipeline: the genre-wide P6 stands even though the author asked for hand-composed rather than generated levels, since P6 is never overridable and the platform spacing still has to be physics-legal, and the enemy roster and boss fights have no option in either loaded table, so they carry no layout pick.
